body:
aida-monitor's six recommendations, verified: five stand, one is already done, and two I filed against the report rather than for it

The operator relayed six recommendations from the aida-monitor project, built by Antigravity against this repo. I reproduced every number here before filing anything. Five drafts are in your inbox: BUG-1286 through BUG-1290. Two of the six came back different from how they were reported, and those are the two worth your attention first.

WHAT I FILED

BUG-1286, terminal events. Confirmed and worse than reported. There is no SpecCompleted or SpecMerged event kind at all. Of 514 closed specs in the feed, exactly ONE ends on a terminal event; 88 end on an event asserting they are still in flight or failed. TASK-1285 is Completed and its last word in the feed is SpecShelved. The gap is where the close happens outside the drain — a batch PR trailer, or the pull auto-bump. This is not a monitor inconvenience: every rounds-to-merge and drain-success number we compute from this feed counts a later-recovered shelve as the final outcome, which means the measurements EPIC-62 is using to decide whether reliability is improving are biased pessimistic. TASK-1294, the rounds-to-merge measurement now in the wave, will read this feed.

BUG-1287, the reaper. Their counts are exact: 30 orphan worktrees, 13 dead agents, and doctor reports 1759 findings including 301 stale remote branches and 8 stale leases. 73 sibling worktree directories, 141 GiB. But their recommendation was "add opportunistic auto-reap", and that shipped as TASK-1177. So I wrote the spec as "classify which of the three reap predicates fails for each of the thirty BEFORE changing the reaper" — because if the failing predicate is "spec not Completed", this is a symptom of BUG-1286 and the fix belongs upstream, not in the reaper.

BUG-1288, read-surface latency. They measured awaiting --json at 10-25 s. I measured 70.2, 71.9 and 77.5 s on three consecutive runs, and status --full at 88.6 s. Their figure was optimistic.

BUG-1289, the format flag. `--format json` returns human prose on `aida status <SPEC>` and TOON on `aida ps`. Also: `aida status <SPEC>` ALREADY synthesises the unified per-spec state their sixth recommendation asks for — status, liveness with the flag-only case, parked reason, next action. The gap is that it has no machine-readable form. So I narrowed their "introduce aida round status" to "give the existing view a JSON shape", explicitly against adding a second verb answering a question we already answer.

BUG-1290, duplicate PhaseEntered. This is the one I would not file as recommended. 412 extra emissions of 2190, yes. But splitting them: 290 are spurious back-to-back pairs a median of 5 seconds apart, and 121 are LEGITIMATE re-entries each preceded by SpecRetried. Their fix — suppress a repeated (spec, run_uuid, phase) at the emit site — would swallow all 121. A phase re-entered four times on one run is the pathology BUG-1268 exists to describe; the cure would hide the disease. The spec instead says find the two call sites double-announcing, and carry an attempt number so a real re-entry is distinguishable by value rather than by what happens to sit next to it in the feed.

WHAT I DID NOT FILE

Their fourth recommendation, make status/list/ps offline-first by default, is already true. Bare `aida status` 0.66 s, `aida list` 0.44 s warm, `aida ps` 0.38 s, `awaiting --notice` 0.93 s. STORY-707 did this. Filing it would have sent an implementer to fix something that works. I mention it because it is the clearest evidence that an outside report needs reproducing rather than transcribing — four of their six numbers were right, one was pessimistic about us, one was optimistic.

ONE THING FOR YOUR GROOMING. BUG-1289 overlaps STORY-1352, the versioned read-only monitor contract, which is queued in the current wave. I filed it separately because the format flag is a plain conformance defect that should be fixed whether or not the contract lands — today the shared --format help says "json = machine JSON" and on these commands that is false. But if you would rather fold it in as acceptance on STORY-1352, that is a reasonable call and it is yours; STORY-1352 has not started yet, so acceptance can still change cleanly.

The monitor doing this at all is the dogfooding result we wanted. It found real defects in our read surfaces within a day of existing, which is the argument for STORY-1352 having a real consumer rather than a hypothetical one.
